# Intake Brief: Herdr downtime audit claim leaves item in-progress/in_review; failed audit strands review-queue items

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher's audit-tier pre-dispatch CAS claim flips a `completed`/`in_review` item's status to `in_progress` while leaving the stage at `in_review`, creating a hybrid state that the audit runner's own inlined `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` table rejects. When the audit then fails (Phase-2 timeout, infra failure), the runner's failure-restore coerces the hybrid to `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, stranding the item one step down — off the review queue, out of the audit tier's selection, and out of the release gate's visibility.

## Users

- **Operator** (runs herdr downtime dispatch): wants audit auto-dispatch to be transparent — no item should silently change state as a side effect of being audited.
- **Producer/reviewer**: wants every `in_review` item to stay on the review queue (observable via `completed`/`in_review`) until a genuine audit verdict or manual action moves it, so infra failures never invisibly remove work from review.
- **Auto-dispatched audit agent** (`/skill:audit <id>`): wants pre-flight guard and pre-audit state capture to see the true pre-claim state (`completed`/`in_review`), not the dispatcher's claim artifact.

User stories:
- As an operator, when herdr auto-dispatches an audit of a `completed`/`in_review` item and the audit fails, the item must remain `completed`/`in_review` so a re-run or manual review can still proceed.
- As a producer, I want no failed audit to ever strand an item at `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, invisible to the review queue and the audit tier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the herdr audit tier dispatches an audit of a `completed`/`in_review` item, the item's observable state (via `wl show`) never becomes `in-progress`/`in_review` as a dispatch artifact — the claim is status- and stage-neutral (or restores the pre-claim state as the single visible state while the audit runs only where the runner itself manages the lifecycle).

- After a failed/interrupted herdr-dispatched audit of a `completed`/`in_review` item (Phase-2 timeout, infra failure, SIGKILL, pane kill), the item is verified back at `completed`/`in_review` via `wl show` readback — never `in-progress`/`plan_complete`, and never left `in_progress`.

- The audit runner's failure-restore and abort-recovery (SIGKILL state-file) paths restore `completed`/`in_review` for review-queue items, including when the captured pre-audit state is the herdr claim hybrid — no coercion to `plan_complete`. Covered by unit + integration tests.

- Double-dispatch protection (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 1: exactly one concurrent pane wins the claim) is preserved; the alternative claim mechanism has its own race-safety test.

- The existing `in-progress`/`in_review` transitional exception in the wl validator (`src/status-stage-validation.ts`) is retained or tightened only in step with the chosen fix (never removed while herdr can still create the hybrid); regression tests for the validator remain green.

- **Testing/validation criterion:** all of the above are covered by meaningful tests (unit + an integration-style dispatch→failed-audit→restore scenario); the full project test suite passes with the changes.

- **Documentation criterion:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `AGENTS.md` (claim pattern), and any relevant skill docs (`/skill:audit` README note on CAS claims).

- **Suite criterion:** full project test suite must pass with the new changes (ContextHub `tests/` + `packages/herdr`); cross-repo audit-runner tests in the owning project where the fix lands.

## Constraints

- **Repo boundary (decided 2026-10-14):** `audit_runner.py` lives in the shared skills install sourced from the SorraAgents repo (`skill/audit`), not this repo. Changes there happen via that repo's own work items (SA work item), linked from here as `Blocked-by`. This bug is the tracking/verification item.
- The dispatch-failure rollback path (`rollbackClaimWorkItem`) already restores `completed`/`in_review` for audit (fetcher.ts `rollbackClaimWorkItem`); it must keep working and be covered.
- `needsProducerReview` removal and the assignee-based scheduling hold are out of scope for the *immediate* bug fix — they belong to epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ (Option A follow-on). This item must not depend on that epic landing.
- Keep the fix surgical: no behaviour change to the other tiers' claims (they legitimately claim `open` items as in_progress) or to the review-queue depth gate.
- The audit runner's own entry claim (in_progress) and the pre-flight guard (needs `--force` for in_progress items) remain as-is unless the chosen fix removes the need for `--force`; if the claim becomes status-neutral, the pre-flight guard no longer trips and the audit no longer needs `--force` — that is desirable, not a regression.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` `claimWorkItem` (L1197) always sets `--status in_progress`; `TIER_EXPECTED.audit = {status:'completed', stage:'in_review'}` (downtime-worker.ts:2385) is only the CAS guard.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `dispatchClaimedTier` (L2943) claims with the tier expectation, then marker, then spawn; rollback on marker/spawn failure restores via `rollbackClaimWorkItem` with the tier's expected state (completed/in_review for audit).
- The wl validator (`src/status-stage-validation.ts`, compiled `dist/status-stage-validation.js:36-48`) already permits `in-progress`/`in_review` as a documented transitional exception for exactly this audit path.
- The audit runner's separate inlined table (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT`, L11894) lacks that exception, so `_coerce_valid_status_stage` (L11931-11937) coerces `in_review → plan_complete` on failure-restore.
- The audit runner success path (`wl update --status completed --stage in_review`) already returns the item to the review queue; only the failure/interrupt path is broken.
- Related completed work proves the edges: WL-0MTYL7DX9000MZOH (retired `in_progress` *stage* claim), SA-0MUIVCJLW000RUC1 (invalid pre-audit combo coercion in audit runner), SA-0MSL1Z1WU005O5IY (pre-flight guard).

## Desired change

Chosen approach (producer decision): **Option A — make the audit-tier claim status-/stage-neutral** so the item stays `completed`/`in_review` through the herdr dispatch claim; the audit runner then captures the true pre-claim state and its failure-restore returns `completed`/`in_review` naturally. The full update is delivered through the existing epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ (status-neutral assignee CAS claim for the audit tier + `needsProducerReview` re-homing), which this item tracks as the root-cause bug. If the epic's full scope cannot proceed, a minimal audit_runner-side mapping (`in-progress`/`in_review` → `completed`/`in_review` on the restore paths, in the owning repo) is the agreed fallback (Option B) but is not the primary path.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `claimWorkItem`: add a status-neutral claim path for the audit tier (produce a `--if-assignee ""`-guarded or equivalent non-status-flipping claim) — needs `wl update --if-assignee` support in `src/commands/update.ts`.
- `src/commands/update.ts` / `src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts` — `--if-assignee` CAS guard support; transitional-exception handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `TIER_EXPECTED` / `dispatchClaimedTier`: wire the audit tier's claim to the status-neutral path.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/claim.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — race-safety + failed-audit-restore regression tests.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (SorraAgents repo) — verify failure-restore + abort-recovery restore `completed`/`in_review`; add the hybrid mapping if the herdr claim still flips status at the time of capture.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents repo) — cross-repo regression tests if the audit-runner mapping changes.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `AGENTS.md` (claim pattern), and the `/skill:audit` docs — update the claim/transitional-exception documentation per AC7.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (producer-confirmed):** Option A (status-neutral claim) is the primary path and is delivered through epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ; this item tracks the root-cause bug and verifies it. If the epic is descoped, the agreed fallback is the audit-runner mapping (Option B).
- **Assumption:** the status-neutral claim requires new `wl update` CAS support (`--if-assignee`) because `--if-status`/`--if-stage` alone cannot make a no-op write exclusive. If that API is rejected, the fallback Option B must be used instead.
- **Risk — assignee residue (P1/P2 in the epic):** clearing discipline and rollback paths must clear the assignee or items ossify as permanently unclaimable. Highest-impact failure mode; the epic owns the mitigation, but this item's verification must assert the audit re-runs after failure.
- **Risk — sync regression guard (P3):** clearing an assignee cross-root may be refused without `--accept-regressions`, resurrecting cleared claims. Must be documented/decided in the epic.
- **Risk — new blocker semantics (P4):** any non-empty assignee becomes a dispatch blocker. Intended as a scheduling hold, but every skill that sets an assignee must clear it on session end; otherwise auto-dispatch silently stops for those items.
- **Risk — validator exception drift:** the wl validator's transitional exception and the audit runner's inlined table are duplicated logic that can drift again; add a test that pins the pair, or centralise.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the pull to also remove `needsProducerReview` and re-home the release gate is high, but that is epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ scope. Any extra opportunity discovered during this item is recorded as a linked work item, not absorbed here.
- **Failure mode if partially fixed:** changing only the herdr claim without the audit runner's abort-recovery path leaves SIGKILL strands at a hybrid state; both paths are covered by the ACs.

## Related work

- Epic **WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ** (Option A: status-neutral assignee CAS claim for audit tier + remove needsProducerReview) — this item is a **tracking/verification umbrella** that **depends-on** the epic (Blocked-by) and is auto-unblocked when the epic completes; the epic carries the full Option A design incl. P1–P8 analysis. Dependency direction corrected 2026-10-14 (producer Q-C).
- **WL-0MTYL7DX9000MZOH** (retired in_progress stage claim fix) — completed; same claim path, different trigger.
- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** (CAS claim RCA) — completed; design point 1 this fix must preserve.
- **SA-0MSL1Z1WU005O5IY** (pre-flight guard) — completed; interacts with the audit claim state.
- **SA-0MUIVCJLW000RUC1** (audit_runner invalid pre-audit combo coercion) — completed; the coercion this bug hits.
- **WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN** (conditional claim + marker exclusion impl) — completed.
- **WL-0MUWKGW9W004QXQZ** (claim skip for done) — completed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Fix approach — (A) herdr status-neutral claim (epic scope), (B) audit_runner restore fix, (C) staged B-now/A-later — which?" — Answer (producer, 2026-10-14): **A** — the status-neutral claim redesign; the epic WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ is the delivery vehicle. Source: interactive intake reply.
- Q2: "Repo boundary — cross-repo acceptable (audit-runner fix in SorraAgents) or ContextHub-only?" — Answer (producer, 2026-10-14): **(a) cross-repo acceptable** — audit_runner changes land in its owning repo's work items, linked from here. Source: interactive intake reply.

## Effort and risk (preliminary)

- **Effort:** Large (cross-repo: herdr claim redesign + `wl update` CAS API + audit-runner lifecycle verification). The narrow fallback (Option B) is Small; the primary Option A path is Large.
- **Risk:** High — touches the CAS claim that prevents duplicate dispatch (WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT), a shared lifecycle owner in another repo, and cross-root sync semantics.

## RM summary (research)

Confirmed the wl validator already allows the hybrid as a documented transitional exception and the audit runner's separate table does not; confirmed the audit runner owns the exit-side lifecycle and lives outside this repo; confirmed no completed item duplicates this bug (SA-0MUIVCJLW000RUC1 fixed the coercion mechanics generally, not the dispatch-claim hybrid); verified `--if-assignee` is not yet a `wl update` flag, so a status-neutral claim requires either that flag or an equivalent CAS mechanism.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MMORPRHK1HR7H36** – Code review: PR #932 (completed)
- **WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV** – Audit-tier downtime dispatch tests (completed)
- **WL-0MTQZ7HZY005GYIQ** – Update grouping logic to remove in_progress from Group N (completed)

# Status-neutral audit-tier claim and guarded rollback (herdr)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator running herdr downtime dispatch, I want the audit-tier claim to change only the assignee, so an audited `completed`/`in_review` item never enters a hybrid state and a failed audit can never strand it off the review queue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Audit-tier claim is status-neutral: item stays completed/in_review through dispatch and failed-audit restore (`wl show` after simulated failure shows completed/in_review).
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] `claimWorkItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) issues `wl update <id> --assignee <agent> --if-status completed --if-stage in_review --if-assignee ""` — it writes no `--status` and no `--stage`.
- [ ] The item reads back as `completed`/`in_review` via `wl show` throughout the claim (no `in-progress`/`in_review` hybrid).
- [ ] `rollbackClaimWorkItem` clears the assignee guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>`, so only this claim's state is reverted.
- [ ] Exactly-one-winner is preserved (the C1 concurrency test passes).
- [ ] `classifyItemForDispatch`/the audit-tier `select*` functions exclude items with a non-empty assignee, so assigning an item to the producer makes the claim fail stale at every tier.
- [ ] Tests cover: claim keeps completed/in_review; concurrent claim single-winner; an assignee-held item is not dispatched.

## Constraints

- **No hybrid status/stage write**: the new claim path must never produce `in-progress`/`in_review`.
- The `--if-assignee ""` guard is the exclusive token; rollback is guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>`.
- Cross-root claim targeting keeps the existing `--worklog-dir` convention.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (`claimWorkItem`, `rollbackClaimWorkItem`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`classifyItemForDispatch`, `select*`, `dispatchClaimedTier`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts`

## Deliverables

Status-neutral claim, guarded rollback, assignee-based selection exclusion, tests.
data.title: Status-neutral audit-tier claim and guarded rollback (herdr)

# Failed-dispatch recovery clears the assignee

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want every dispatch failure path to release the claim's assignee, so a marker-write-failed or spawn-failed dispatch never strands an item as permanently unclaimable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Failed dispatch (marker-write-failed / spawn-failed) clears assignee and leaves item re-selectable.
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] The marker-write-failed recovery path clears the assignee guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>` and leaves the item re-selectable.
- [ ] The spawn-failed recovery path clears the assignee guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>` and leaves the item re-selectable.
- [ ] After each failure mode, `wl show` shows `completed`/`in_review` with an empty assignee.
- [ ] Tests cover both failure modes and assert re-selectability by the audit tier.
- [ ] No dispatch failure mode can leave a non-empty assignee behind.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`rollbackClaimForFailure`, recovery/stranding paths)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts`

## Deliverables

Recovery-path change plus tests.

# Assignee-hold scheduling convention and producer sentinel

## Goal (user story)

As a producer, I want an explicit per-item way to pause automatic scheduling — by assigning the item to myself — that does not rely on a magic DB flag, with a well-known sentinel value the release gate can recognise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Assign item to producer ⇒ no tier auto-dispatches it (claims fail stale at every tier) — the scheduling hold works.
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] Epic open question Q2 is answered and recorded: the literal producer-hold value is a reserved, well-known value equal to the producer's wl identity (self-describing, reusable by the release gate). **Recommended:** reserved identity value, exact literal confirmed with the producer.
- [ ] The convention is documented: a non-empty assignee means "intentionally held from auto-dispatch"; assigning to the producer is the per-item pause switch.
- [ ] Every ContextHub/SorraAgents assignee writer is audited (intake, plan, implement, triage, delegate `@github-copilot`, `status_lifecycle`) and clears the assignee on session end; `status_lifecycle`'s failure-exit already clears it.
- [ ] A test proves that clearing a claim's assignee makes the item dispatchable again (hold released).
- [ ] Correctness risk R1 is addressed by the clearing-discipline audit (no writer silently suppresses auto-dispatch).

## Constraints

- The sentinel must not collide with real agent identities.
- Must not strand in-flight implement/plan/intake claims: only session-end clearing is added.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents)
- `./AGENTS.md` (draft claim/hold pattern; finalised in C12)

## Deliverables

Sentinel decision, convention documentation, clearing-discipline changes, test.
data.title: Assignee-hold scheduling convention and producer sentinel

# Audit runner: clear assignee on terminal verdicts and preserve completed/in_review on failure

## Cross-repo note

This work item is implemented in the **SorraAgents** repo (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`); a SorraAgents (SA) work item is created there and linked from this epic. AGENTS.md forbids editing `skill/` dirs without explicit instruction.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the audit runner to release its assignee claim on every terminal outcome and never coerce a review-queue item out of `completed`/`in_review` on failure, so auto-dispatched audits leave no residue and re-runs still dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Success path clears assignee; legacy residue cleared by a one-time migration/script; audit re-runs still dispatch.
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] On the success ('yes') verdict path the runner clears the assignee (`--assignee ""`), retains `completed`/`in_review`, and applies the producer hold required by policy.
- [ ] On the failure-restore path the runner restores `completed`/`in_review` and clears the assignee — the inlined `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` coercion of `in_review → plan_complete` is no longer reachable for review-queue items.
- [ ] The SIGKILL abort-recovery (state-file) path restores `completed`/`in_review` and clears the assignee.
- [ ] On the 'no' verdict path the runner clears the assignee.
- [ ] Unit + integration tests cover each terminal path, including the captured-pre-audit-state = status-neutral-claim case.
- [ ] A SorraAgents work item exists for this change and is linked as related work.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (SorraAgents)
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents)

## Deliverables

audit_runner.py changes, tests, linked SA work item.
data.title: Audit runner: clear assignee on terminal verdicts, preserve completed/in_review on failure

# One-time legacy assignee residue cleanup

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the existing assignee residue cleaned up once, idempotently and narrowly, so the review queue drains instead of ossifying under 700+ stale producer holds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An idempotent script clears assignee residue on the ~698 completed + ~7 in_review audit-hold items only; it never clears in-flight implement/plan/intake claims.
- [ ] A dry-run mode prints the affected items and counts before any write.
- [ ] Re-running the script is a no-op (no further writes reported).
- [ ] The script is tested against a fixture database covering: audit-hold residue (cleared), in-flight claim (untouched), and already-clean items (untouched).
- [ ] Ordering is documented: the script runs **after** the code change ships (status-neutral claim + assignee-based selection, C4/C6).

## Constraints

- Idempotent; scoped to audit-hold residue; never touches `needsProducerReview` (removed separately).
- Must not run until C4/C6 have shipped (documented in the work item).

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/cleanup-assignee-residue.ts` (new cleanup script)
- `tests/cleanup-assignee-residue.test.ts` (fixture-DB tests)

## Deliverables

Cleanup script, dry-run mode, tests.

# Docs, AGENTS.md claim pattern and end-to-end verification

## Goal (user story)

As an agent or maintainer, I want the claim/hold convention and the new CLI surface documented, and the whole flow verified end to end, so the change is operable and discoverable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Full test suite passes; CLI.md / docs updated; AGENTS.md claim pattern updated.
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` (ContextHub and SorraAgents) claim pattern is updated to the status-neutral assignee CAS plus the assignee-hold convention.

data.description:
# Herdr selection list: `Blocked By` metadata line flickers endlessly on blocked items (WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP)

**Headline:** The Herdr metadata panel has two live render states for a blocked item (async `Blocked By` lookup pending → line absent; resolved → line present), and `doRefresh()` clears the per-item blocker cache on *every* list refresh, so frequent refresh triggers (DB-change watch, auto-sync counter bumps, `wl next` re-sorts) re-flip the panel between the two states endlessly. Fix: make the resolved state survive refreshes and invalidate only when the item's dependency edges can actually change.

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work-item selection list, selecting a dependency-blocked item makes the metadata panel's `Blocked By` line appear for a moment, then disappear for a moment, then reappear — repeating endlessly. Selecting a blocked item is therefore visually noisy and leaves the "what is this blocked on?" answer (added by WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8) unreliable at a glance.

## RCA (root cause analysis)

There are two distinct render states for the work-item preview, and the live loop flips between them on every refresh:

- **Path A — metadata panel, resolved:** `formatMetadataPanel(..., metaBlockedBy)` renders one `Blocked By` row per active blocker. `metaBlockedBy` is produced by `resolveMetaBlockers()` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), which resolves asynchronously via `fetchBlockersForItem()` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`; spawns `wl dep list <id> --json` plus one `wl show` per candidate blocker) and caches the result in an in-memory `blockerCache` keyed by item ID.
- **Path B — metadata panel, unresolved:** until the lookup lands (or after the cache is dropped), `resolveMetaBlockers()` returns `undefined`, `state.metaBlockedBy` is `null`, and the panel renders **without** the `Blocked By` rows. A follow-up `render()` is scheduled from the fetch's `.finally()`, so the line pops in ~one lookup latency later (~0.5–2 s for two spawned `wl` processes).

**Why it repeats endlessly:** `doRefresh()` calls `blockerCache.clear()` on **every** list refresh (`worklist.ts`, in the refresh path). Every cache clear re-introduces the unresolved frame for the full async lookup, then the `.finally(render())` flips it back. Refreshes fire far more often than the 30 s tick in a live workspace:

- the DB-change watch (`db-change.ts`) reacts within ~150 ms (debounce) to any `wl` state-counter bump — real agent writes, and *every successful auto-sync* (`src/commands/sync.ts` bumps the read-cache counter) — each feeding `requestWatchRefresh → doRefresh`;
- the auto-sync task itself runs `doRefresh(false)` unconditionally on its cadence;
- `wl next` re-sorts bump the counter when the dispatcher runs it (`src/commands/next.ts`).

So under sustained write/sync traffic the line alternates on/off continuously — the reported "for a moment… disappear for a moment… repeat endlessly". The design intent ("an unresolved item renders without rows and a follow-up render shows them") assumed a one-time transition per selection; invalidating the cache on every refresh breaks that assumption.

**Secondary inconsistency (the "other path" the report refers to):** only the list-mode metadata panel renders `Blocked By`. The **detail view** (`formatDetailContent`, the other work-item preview render path) builds its metadata table from `buildMetaRows()` without blocker rows, and the hover tooltip (`formatTooltipLines`) also omits them — so the two preview render paths have already diverged (one has the line, the other does not).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** browsing the Herdr selection list. Story: "When I select a blocked item, I want the `Blocked By` line to appear once and stay put until the data actually changes — not flash on and off."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Selecting a dependency-blocked item shows the `Blocked By` line stably: once resolved, no render frame drops the line on subsequent auto-refresh ticks, DB-change (watcher) refreshes, or auto-sync cycles; observed over ≥3 consecutive refresh cycles with the DB otherwise idle.
- [ ] List refreshes never blank the panel: a refresh reuses the last known blockers for the same selected item (or resolves from the freshly fetched payload) instead of re-running the async lookup and rendering an unresolved frame; there is at most one spawn of `wl dep list` (and enrichment) per item until its edges can actually change (selection change, or a refresh that changed the item's dependency set).
- [ ] The live loop is bounded and self-terminating: a blocked item under simulated refresh + counter/watch events ends in a stable frame set (exactly one unresolved→resolved transition per selection), never an oscillating pair.
- [ ] Unblocked items are unaffected: their metadata panel output is byte-for-byte unchanged; headings, list navigation, description preview, and `m`/`M` scroll clamping (including `metadataPanelContentHeight` with `metaBlockedBy`) behave as before.
- [ ] The two preview render paths are reconciled: the detail view either renders the same `Blocked By` rows as the list metadata panel, or this divergence is explicitly documented out of scope with a code comment — but the report's "two paths, one has the line, one does not" inconsistency must be resolved one way or the other.
- [ ] Fail-open behaviour is preserved: a failed `wl dep list`/`wl show` still yields no `Blocked By` rows and never breaks rendering or navigation.
- [ ] Regression tests cover: stable frames across repeated refreshes for a blocked selection; single-flight/no re-spawn for an unchanged selection; cache reuse semantics; and the detail-view parity decision.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Display-only change**: the fix must not create or mutate dependency edges, and must not change list-data shape for non-panel consumers.
- **Render path must never block**: keep synchronous rendering; any resolution stays async but never causes a visual regression to an earlier frame.
- **Reuse existing helpers**: `isActiveBlocker()` (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`) and `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`).
- **No extra `wl` spawns on refresh**: refresh must not re-run the per-item blocker lookup when nothing about that item's edges changed.
- **Scope**: primary fix is the selection-list metadata panel flicker. Detail-view/tooltip parity is secondary and decided within this item (fix or explicitly documented out of scope).

## Existing state

- `resolveMetaBlockers` + `blockerCache`/`blockerInFlight` (async, per-selection, cached by item ID, cleared in `doRefresh`) — introduced by WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8.
- `formatMetadataPanel`/`buildMetadataPanelLines` render `Blocked By` rows from the `blockedBy` argument; `metadataPanelContentHeight` shares the same content so the scroll clamp matches the renderer (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8).
- The DB-change watch (`db-change.ts`) deliberately watches only the state-counter file to avoid the WAL/`-shm` self-sustaining loop (WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN); the counter is bumped by every `wl` write, successful `wl sync`, and `wl next` re-sort byproduct (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`) — the refresh triggers that drive the flicker cadence.
- Loop-free refresh machinery (single-flight + trailing coalescing in `doRefresh`, debounced `requestWatchRefresh`, scheduler at `scheduler.ts`) is in place and must be preserved.

## Desired change

Make the `Blocked By` state transition idempotent and non-regressive per selection:

1. Keep the renderer's two states (with/without rows) but stop re-clearing the cache on unrelated refreshes — invalidate only when the selected item's dependency edges can have changed (new selection, or a refresh that changes the item), or resolve blockers from the fresh payload so the resolved state survives refresh atomically.
2. Cache the in-flight lookup itself so repeated refreshes never race/duplicate the spawn, and re-render from cache thereafter.
3. Decide and implement detail-view parity (render the same rows or document the divergence).

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveMetaBlockers`, `blockerCache.clear()` in `doRefresh`, render-loop wiring of `metaBlockedBy`; `formatDetailContent`/`formatTooltipLines` for parity.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchBlockersForItem` (lookup + per-edge enrichment); consider promise-level memoisation.
- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts` — the refresh triggers whose counter bumps set the flicker cadence (context; not expected to change).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-blockers.test.ts` — regression tests.

## Related work

- WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8 — "Show what an item is blocked on": parent feature that introduced the flickering async render path (regression source).
- WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN — "…DB-change watch" producer-rejection fix: the loop-free state-counter contract any fix must respect.
- WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA / WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W — read-cache + sync-heartbeat work that bumps the counter on sync (refresh frequency context).
- WL-0MSBVBNGH002RDP5 — prior "momentary collapse on refresh (flicker)" bug: the refresh path must stay atomic.
- WL-0MT9ZJF28004UJ28 — description-preview caching in the same metadata panel (precedent for cache-invalidation semantics).

### Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MQP303A900780R0** – Escape key in Pi TUI work item detail view should navigate back to selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MT1JH1HN004JP1F** – T5: Metadata panel group info on heading (completed)
- **WL-0MQEJ2SLX009X17O** – Add risk and effort T-shirt size icons to Pi TUI work item selection list (completed)

Repository file matches: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (keyword overlap only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the reported flicker is the list-mode metadata panel alternating between the unresolved and resolved `Blocked By` frames on repeated refreshes; the "two paths" wording also matches the detail view missing the line. Both readings are covered in the ACs.
- **Assumption:** refreshes in the reporter's environment were frequent enough (live workspace with agent writes / auto-sync / dispatcher `wl next`) to make the per-refresh blanking look continuous. The fix must be robust even under a fast refresh loop.
- **Risk — over-invalidation fix:** caching forever can show stale blockers after a real dependency change; the invalidation rule must distinguish "nothing changed" (reuse) from "item changed" (re-resolve).
- **Risk — spawn amplification:** the current code already spawns `wl dep list` + up to N× `wl show` per lookup; the fix must not add spawns to the refresh path.
- **Scope-creep risk:** detail-view/tooltip parity is tempting to expand; keep it to fix-or-document per AC5. Extra ideas should be tracked as separate work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed report plus repository investigation were sufficient to define the problem and the measurable acceptance criteria.

- Q (implicit): "Which code path renders the `Blocked By` line, and why does it flicker?" — Answer (investigation): two live states in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveMetaBlockers()` returns `undefined` while the async `fetchBlockersForItem()` lookup is pending (line absent) and the cached array once it lands (line present); `doRefresh()` clears `blockerCache` on every refresh, so each refresh re-enters the absent state. Source: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`resolveMetaBlockers`, `blockerCache.clear()` in `doRefresh`) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (`fetchBlockersForItem`).
- Q (implicit): "Do the two preview render paths differ?" — Answer (investigation): yes — list-mode `formatMetadataPanel` renders `Blocked By`; the detail view `formatDetailContent` (and the hover tooltip `formatTooltipLines`) build metadata from `buildMetaRows()` only and omit it. Source: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Q (implicit): "What sets the flicker cadence?" — Answer (investigation + empirical check): the DB-change watch/react + auto-sync (successful `wl sync` bumps the read-cache state counter) + `wl next` re-sort byproduct bumps; verified with `wl list`/`wl show`/`wl dep list --json` that plain reads do not bump the counter. Source: `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/next.ts`.

Implementation notes (commit b9a6ae9c):

- Root cause confirmed: the form-dialog onSubmit in worklist.ts called opts.onCommand(finalCmd, model) with 2 args, dropping the resolved openPane flag, so a-r fell back to openPane ?? true and opened a pane.
- Fix: extracted the existing arity rules into a shared invokeOnCommand() helper and routed the form-dialog path through it (openPane + onRefresh + focus), mirroring resolveAndRouteCommand/executeResolvedCommand exactly. No new flag or dispatch mechanism.
- Test placement deviation: regression tests live in tests/unit/form-dialog-open-pane.test.ts (not packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts as predicted). The canonical agent suite in .pi/test-config.json runs only tests/cli and tests/unit; placing the tests there guarantees they execute in the finish gate and the audit cache. The packages/herdr omission is the pre-existing tracked gap WL-0MUU173V8008IA5E.
- The worklog cache recorded exit_code 0 for both configured suites (tests/cli, tests/unit) and for packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts (run via a temporary local test type); the finish gate's first attempt was failed only by the live-repo mutation guard tripping on refs moved by other concurrent agents, not by a test failure. Re-run on the green cache succeeded.
- Out of scope: adding open_pane:false to c-q (tracked by WL-0MV6J5JXL002D8C4).
